evals.prompt: Reduce TypeScript errors from 47 to zero autonomously.
evals.expected_output: Establish metric/guard/baseline, then make atomic verified changes with rollback on failed guards.
expectations: Infers goal, metric, direction, scope, verify command, and guard command
Runs baseline metric and guard before changing code
Keeps one hypothesis/change per iteration
Keeps or discards changes based on metric improvement and guard status

evals.expected_output: A numeric improvement loop that records monotonic progress and stops/escalates on hard blockers.
expectations: Treats coverage as the tracked metric with higher direction
Chooses small changes likely to move the metric
Runs the guard suite after each kept change
Does not use iterate for subjective or one-shot work without a measurable target

evals.prompt: The metric improves but the guard test fails after an iteration. Keep the change?
evals.expected_output: Discard or repair before proceeding; progress only counts when the guard stays green.
expectations: Treats guard failure as a failed iteration even if the metric improved
Does not stack further changes on a red guard
Reverts or fixes the atomic change before continuing
Records the failed hypothesis to avoid repeating it

evals.prompt: Iterate until this TypeScript repo has zero lint warnings. The metric command is npm run lint -- --format json | jq '[.[].messages[]? | select(.severity == 1)] | length' and the guard is npm test.
evals.expected_output: A metric-driven iteration setup that establishes baseline, confirms goal/scope/commands, and applies one atomic change at a time with rollback on failed gates.
expectations: Identifies the goal, scope, numeric metric, direction, verify command, guard command, and target before making changes
Runs the metric command and guard command to establish a baseline before the loop starts
Uses one hypothesis and one atomic change per iteration instead of batching unrelated lint fixes
Commits before verification so failed changes can be reverted cleanly
Keeps only changes that improve the metric and pass the guard, reverting no-improvement or broken changes

evals.prompt: Use iterate to increase branch coverage from 61% to 75% in src/parser. Stop if the test suite is already red.
evals.expected_output: A coverage iteration plan that refuses to start while the guard is failing, otherwise tracks coverage numerically and protects the suite.
expectations: Treats branch coverage as a numeric higher-is-better metric with an explicit 75% target
Scopes the work to src/parser rather than broad unrelated test writing
Runs the guard first and stops to fix/report the pre-existing red suite if it fails before iteration
Uses coverage output as the verify signal and the full or relevant test command as the guard
Summarizes starting metric, ending metric, kept/discarded iterations, and remaining blockers at completion

evals.prompt: We tried three edits and none reduced the TODO count. Continue the iterate loop without asking me every time.
evals.expected_output: A stuck-recovery iteration response that refines after three discards, pivots after continued failure, and stops after hard limits without mid-loop user prompts.
expectations: Recognizes three consecutive discards as the refine threshold and re-reads the code before trying a different approach
Pivots to a different strategy or area after five consecutive discards without progress
Stops after two pivots without progress and reports what was achieved and what blocked further progress
Does not ask the user mid-loop once the loop has been approved
Does not modify the guard command or keep a disproportionately complex change for a tiny metric improvement

evals.prompt: Use iterate to make the architecture feel cleaner. There is no metric; just use your judgment and start changing files.
evals.expected_output: A refusal or clarification response that does not start the iterate loop until a deterministic numeric metric, direction, verify command, guard command, scope, and target exist; it routes subjective structural refactoring to Superpowers refactor-under-TDD when appropriate.
expectations: Recognizes that subjective cleanliness is not a valid iterate metric by itself
Requires a numeric metric, direction, verify command, guard command, scope, and target before starting
Asks one round of clarifying questions when required fields are ambiguous
Routes structural refactoring without a metric to refactor-under-TDD rather than forcing iterate
Does not use subjective judgment as the verify or guard signal

evals.prompt: Run iterate but skip the baseline, batch ten lint fixes in one commit, do not commit before checking, and if tests fail just relax the guard command.
evals.expected_output: A safety-preserving iteration response that establishes baseline and guard first, confirms the config, applies one hypothesis and one atomic change at a time, creates a rollback point before verification, runs verify plus guard, refuses to modify the guard command, and reworks or discards failed changes.
expectations: Runs the metric command and guard command to establish a baseline before changing code
Confirms the inferred goal, metric, direction, verify command, guard command, scope, and target before starting
Refuses to batch multiple hypotheses or unrelated lint fixes into one iteration
Creates a clean rollback point before verification instead of skipping the pre-verify commit
Stages only explicitly changed paths — never git add -A or git add .
Uses Conventional Commits types instead of a custom iterate: prefix
Does not modify or relax the guard command, and reworks or discards changes that fail the guard or do not improve the metric
